messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus) is a prescription GLP-1 medication used for weight loss and weight management, type 2 diabetes treatment, or to reduce the risk of chronic kidney disease and major cardiovascular events in certain patients with type 2 diabetes. Semaglutide (Wegovy) is also used to treat metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), without cirrhosis of the liver.
Semaglutide injections are self-administered once weekly as an injection under the skin, and semaglutide pills are taken once daily.
Semaglutide works by reducing appetite, delaying gastric emptying, increasing insulin release, and lowering the amount of glucagon released. Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist that mimics the behavior of the GLP-1 hormone, which is naturally released after eating.
Semaglutide brand names are Ozempic, Rybelsus, and Wegovy, all made by Novo Nordisk. There is no generic semaglutide available. Semaglutide FDA approval was first granted on December 5, 2017, for the brand Ozempic.
Each semaglutide brand or formulation is FDA-approved for specific conditions and patient populations.
Triples: [["Semaglutide", "has brand names", "Ozempic"], ["Semaglutide", "has brand names", "Wegovy"], ["Semaglutide", "has brand names", "Rybelsus"], ["Semaglutide", "manufactured by", "Novo Nordisk"], ["Semaglutide", "has generic availability", "not available"], ["Semaglutide", "has mechanism of action", "reducing appetite"], ["Semaglutide", "has mechanism of action", "delaying gastric emptying"], ["Semaglutide", "has mechanism of action", "increasing insulin release"], ["Semaglutide", "has mechanism of action", "lowering glucagon release"], ["Semaglutide", "is a", "GLP-1 receptor agonist"], ["Semaglutide", "mimics", "GLP-1 hormone"], ["Semaglutide", "treats", "type 2 diabetes"], ["Semaglutide", "used for", "weight loss"], ["Semaglutide", "used for", "weight management"], ["Semaglutide", "reduces risk of", "chronic kidney disease"], ["Semaglutide", "reduces risk of", "major cardiovascular events"], ["Semaglutide", "treats", "metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis"], ["Semaglutide", "has administration instruction", "injections once weekly under the skin"], ["Semaglutide", "has administration instruction", "pills once daily"], ["Semaglutide", "has fda approval date", "December 5, 2017"], ["Semaglutide", "has specific condition approval", "type 2 diabetes"], ["Semaglutide", "has specific condition approval", "weight loss"], ["Semaglutide", "has specific condition approval", "weight management"], ["Semaglutide", "has specific condition approval", "metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis"], ["Semaglutide", "has specific population approval", "patients with type 2 diabetes"], ["Semaglutide", "has specific population approval", "without cirrhosis of the liver"]]
Relations: ["has administration instruction", "has brand names", "has fda approval date", "has generic availability", "has mechanism of action", "has specific condition approval", "has specific population approval", "is a", "manufactured by", "mimics", "reduces risk of", "treats", "used for"]
Answer:

completion:
has administration instruction: The subject drug is administered according to the instructions specified by the object entity.  
has brand names: The subject drug is marketed under the brand names listed in the object entity.  
has fda approval date: The subject drug received formal approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on the date specified by the object entity.  
has generic availability: The subject drug is either available or not available in generic form as specified by the object entity.  
has mechanism of action: The subject drug exerts its therapeutic effect through the biological process or physiological change specified by the object entity.  
has specific condition approval: The subject drug is FDA-approved for treating the medical condition specified by the object entity.  
has specific population approval: The subject drug is FDA-approved for use in the patient population specified by the object entity.  
is a: The subject drug belongs to the pharmacological category or class specified by the object entity.  
manufactured by: The subject drug is produced or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.  
mimics: The subject drug functions similarly to the biological molecule or hormone specified by the object entity.  
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical condition or event specified by the object entity.  
treats: The subject drug is used to manage or treat the medical condition specified by the object entity.  
used for: The subject drug is indicated for the therapeutic purpose or application specified by the object entity.
